races.name: Glass Times EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Flat Out Flat Glass Solutions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who recorded his sole similar-going win on Soft — headgear (hood+p noted) and a 10-day return after a 1st on Soft are positive flags; Jack Callan rides and the horse will need a true enough gallop to deliver from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Dapper Guest has one win in his last six starts and ranks seventh of nine on our figures, making him hard to fancy in what looks a competitive contest, though he does return on a short ten-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going in his favour.

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who won over 7f on Soft most recently — Simon Dow's filly has a 2/8 T14 record showing yard is firing; 56 days off is the main query but she sets the tactical agenda here and controls the race shape entirely.
runners_data.comment: Musical Angel shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and she has experience of today's trip and going to call on; the main concern is whether 56 days off the track has left her short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Uppercase
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner over 7f on Good to Soft and Good — Harry Eustace's 0/17 T14 is a concern but the horse's own form line is excellent (1/7f/SOF, 1/7f/GOO); prominent style suits the race shape and she gets close coverage of the leader naturally.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures and rated below his official mark, Uppercase is hard to fancy despite winning twice in his last five starts, most recently a well-beaten eighth; he has run over today's trip and going before, and stall one could prove interesting.

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a headgear change (ht noted) and a 2nd at 8f on Tapeta as best recent form — all five recent runs on Good or Tapeta with no recent wins; needs the pace to collapse which is unlikely given Musical Angel's control.
runners_data.comment: Daring Legend shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, and a second six starts back underlines his ability to hit the frame; he has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 80 makes him a clear danger, though his tendency to go unplaced in between limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Authentic prominent racer who won over 7f Good and placed on Soft; Eve Johnson Houghton has a strong 3/36 T14 rate and the horse's 10-day turnaround from a placed run on Soft suggests she is in good nick and ready to press the leader.
runners_data.comment: Silver Trumpet arrives on the back of a second last time out and a win three starts back, boasting experience over today's trip and going and a sharp 10-day turnaround that suggests he is in good heart; the 136 lb burden from stall nine is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Cuban Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly raced mare with placed form over 7f Good — a genuine hold-up performer by nature but absorbed into the midfield map because the field's rear is congested; Isobelle Chalmers claims 7lb, and the style-fit discount applies here given she is unlikely to race in her preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Cuban Lady has been consistently placed in recent starts, second last time out and third two starts back, but she remains winless in her last five and carries 135 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Three wins in last five starts all on Good ground — Cieren Fallon's booking is a positive and the horse is clearly progressive, but all recent wins are on a faster surface and the step to Soft is an unproven query; hold-up style needs a genuinely honest pace.
runners_data.comment: Norcross Brow arrives in good heart, a winner three times in his last six starts and a close second last time out, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour. Carrying 134 lb from stall four, he rates the confident pick on overall profile.

runners_data.name: Galileo Island
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has placed at 7f and 8f on Good with best form over this trip — 68 days off is notable and T14 of 1/22 is modest; the gelding showed pace figures of 3/7f/GOO recently and can sit in a comfortable stalking spot.
runners_data.comment: Galileo Island shows some encouragement with a third last time out and a second four starts back, but he is winless in his last five starts and returns after a 68-day absence behind a trainer who has been badly out of form recently, sending out just one winner from 22 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Euphonia
runners_data.note: Won twice (Soft and Good) over 7f but is a true hold-up performer pushed into a midfield map position given the rear-heavy field — Ed Walker's 7/44 T14 is the best trainer stat in the race; 70 days off is the fitness question and the style displacement makes her chance structurally harder to realise.
runners_data.comment: Euphonia's two wins in her last six starts offer some hope, and she has run over today's trip before, but back-to-back finishes of sixth and ninth since those victories leave little to work with, and our figures rank her last of nine here.

races.paceDynamic: Musical Angel is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press her for the lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Soft ground at Epsom's seven furlongs. Silver Trumpet and Uppercase are the likeliest horses to sit just off her in the prominent positions, creating a relatively compressed early tempo rather than a scorching pace — sustainable enough that Musical Angel could conceivably hold on, but also not truly punishing for closers. Dapper Guest, Norcross Brow, and Daring Legend will track from midfield to rear, needing the pace to have taken enough toll on the principals to allow late runs. This shape favours prominent racers who can travel into the race without burning fuel — horses that sit within two or three lengths of the leader and pounce off the final bend will be best placed, as a truly contested honest gallop never develops. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; Cuban Lady and Euphonia are genuine closers by nature but are shown in midfield — Silver Trumpet and Uppercase, as authentic prominent types, are most likely to secure those positions ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Musical Angel Controls Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel gets an uncontested lead and sets a sustainable Good to Soft tempo that suits her stamina.
scenarios.body: Musical Angel dictates every yard of the race, controlling fractions through Epsom's straight seven furlongs, and her rivals lack the early pace to pressure her into a fast enough gallop to drain her reserves; Simon Dow's filly has already won on Soft ground over 7f and her form figures on similar going read 1W1P. Silver Trumpet and Uppercase, sitting just off the pace, are the first to challenge but are at risk of being left chasing a horse with lengths in hand turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel is swallowed up by Silver Trumpet and Uppercase in the final two furlongs as a genuine honest pace develops.
scenarios.body: Silver Trumpet's recent Soft-ground win and Uppercase's consecutive wins on Good to Soft (1/7f/SOF and 1/7f/GOO) make both well-suited to pressing the leader home and finishing strongly; the slightly testing ground rewards those who have proven stamina over this trip on this surface. Uppercase in particular, with two consecutive wins and positive trainer stats on the day, has the profile of a horse peaking into form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to leave the front runners vulnerable and Norcross Brow or Dapper Guest storm home late.
scenarios.body: Norcross Brow's excellent recent form — three wins in his last five, all on Good or better — is a mild concern on the softer ground, but his class figures and Cieren Fallon's ability to judge pace make him the likeliest beneficiary if the race sets up for closers; Dapper Guest's single-win record on Soft is a genuine positive and Jack Callan's horse ran a career-best 1st on Soft going in his most recent run. This scenario requires the pace to have been stronger than Musical Angel's tactical control usually allows — a lower-probability shape given the race structure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Reach Midfield And Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cuban Lady or Euphonia manage to push forward from their natural hold-up roles and find an unexpected gap at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Both Cuban Lady and Euphonia are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield because of the field's configuration — they are unlikely to get the ground they need to deliver a classic late run, and their style fit scores of 0.92 and 0.93 reflect racing out of role; Euphonia has wins on Soft and Good and Ed Walker's 14-day strike rate of 7/44 shows live form, but the structural disadvantage of this scenario makes it the least probable shape in this race.

watchPoints.text: Musical Angel's splits in the first two furlongs will determine everything — if she gets completely unchallenged she could control fractions to the point where prominent horses like Uppercase and Silver Trumpet face an impossible task to close her down.

Norcross Brow has won three of his last five but all on Good ground — watch whether the Good to Soft conditions blunt his finishing kick, as Cieren Fallon may try to compensate by moving earlier than ideal.

Cuban Lady and Euphonia are both true hold-up types racing structurally out of role in this field configuration — if either drifts back to their natural position at the rear they face a significant challenge, and punters backing them for a late swoop should be aware of the redistribution.

Uppercase's trainer Harry Eustace shows 0/17 in the 14-day window — worth monitoring in-running to see if the horse travels with its usual fluency or looks flat, as trainer form can be an early-race tell.

Galileo Island's 68-day absence and Tom Ward's modest T14 rate of 1/22 mean race-fitness is a legitimate query — watch how Pierre-Louis Jamin places him early; if the horse is short of peak fitness he may be covered up and only a threat if the pace collapses late.

races.name: Chigwell Group - The Trade's Front Runner Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Moonrunner
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose two placed efforts in soft or standard-to-slow going show she handles cut in the ground; Charlie Fellowes yard form is modest at T14 (1/16) but she is well drawn to attack late if the pace holds, though she may find the tempo too steady to fully deploy her finish.
runners_data.comment: Moonrunner shaped with real promise when second three starts back and arrives here fresh on 19 days' rest, with experience over today's trip and our rating of 83 suggesting he holds strong claims; the risk is he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing hold-up type who has placed on soft twice in recent outings and has strong soft-ground credentials in this company; Dylan Cunha has a busy book (T14 2/26) and Jack Callan's booking is workmanlike — soft going suits but Patrol needs a proper gallop to get home.
runners_data.comment: Patrol has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 134 lb from stall three, he looks the one to beat despite being yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has recorded a win and two places in soft-adjacent conditions; Jim Boyle's yard is live at T14 (1/14), Pat Cosgrave is a booking that commands respect at Epsom, and the step back to 1m2f from recent 10f efforts looks ideal for a horse who stays this trip well.
runners_data.comment: Carnival Day has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, finishing third two of his last five outings, and returns here fit on 13 days' rest having already experienced today's trip and conditions; the concern is he remains winless in this recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer whose true style is at the back of the field — pressure of numbers means he is likely to race closer to midfield than is ideal; William Knight's yard is in form (T14 5/14) and he has a win to his name on good ground, but the style compromise must temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Beach Point won last time out and has run over today's distance and going, giving him a solid platform, though he has found the top four his ceiling for much of his recent starts and must shoulder 134 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Skibo
runners_data.note: Placed in softer conditions once from limited soft-ground starts; his true preference is to race from off the pace, but with so many genuine hold-up types in the field he may find himself racing somewhere in midfield rather than his natural rear position, which will reduce the effectiveness of his late run.
runners_data.comment: Skibo shaped with promise when third and second in consecutive starts not long ago, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid profile at 132 lb from stall 2; the concern is that he has drifted to eighth and seventh in his last two outings, so recovering that earlier form is the key ask.

runners_data.name: Barry's Boy
runners_data.note: Has won over shorter at Sandown and placed from the back, but Denis Coakley's yard has drawn a blank at T14 (0/9) and 28 days off raises a fitness question; a true hold-up horse who will be squeezed toward midfield by the crowded rear, his trip and going profile at 1m2f on soft is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Second two starts back gives Barry's Boy an obvious platform, but he was beaten into sixth last time out and that ninth three starts back is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 132 lb from stall six, and the ratings suggest he is a shade ahead of his official mark.

runners_data.name: Thankyou Baroness
runners_data.note: 195 days off the track makes fitness a serious concern regardless of other factors; a hold-up type whose single soft-ground placing came over 12f and whose trainer has only one runner in the past fortnight — the long absence and redistribution away from her natural rear position compound the risk.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into sixth last time out and winless in her last four starts, Thankyou Baroness also returns after a 195-day absence, making her hard to fancy; a win five starts back and experience over today's trip are modest consolations.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Has headgear (ht) and is a genuine hold-up type who will end up racing in midfield given the crowded back division; Cieren Fallon is an excellent booking and Super Hit's two recent wins on good ground are encouraging, but the soft ground is a query (1/15 on similar going) and the style displacement is a mild negative.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and seventh two starts back, Super Hit has disappointed in his most recent efforts after winning four starts back, and our figures rank him ninth of ten here, making him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and the race-shaper; Mark Hoad's yard has no runners in the T14 window and Liam Wright claims 3lbs, making this a modestly-resourced lead bid — but Bobacious has won over 10f on good-to-soft and an unchallenged lead at OR 65 could prove highly influential.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Bobacious is hard to fancy after finishing seventh last time out, and his overall recent record of one win in his last six starts offers little encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 17-day break.

runners_data.name: Yokkell
runners_data.note: A 47-day break and a 7-year-old's tendency to be inconsistent are concerns; a hold-up horse by nature who will be pushed into midfield by the glut of closers, Yokkell has placed three times at 10-12f on good ground but lacks the soft-ground evidence to inspire confidence — Adrian Wintle's T14 strike rate (1/19) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Yokkell won two starts back but has posted a sixth since, and 47 days off the track is a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going before, and her rating of 72 gives her a small edge over her official mark, though she is up against it from a midfield draw in four.

races.paceDynamic: Bobacious is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, unchallenged for the lead, will be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop on good-to-soft ground over 1m2f at Epsom. With no other genuine pace-setter to press him, Bobacious can set whatever tempo suits him — likely a moderate early clip that stretches into a more testing final two furlongs on the soft-ish surface, creating a race that could reward a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace rather than one making up significant ground late. The hold-up brigade — Moonrunner, Patrol, Carnival Day, Beach Point, Skibo, Barry's Boy, Thankyou Baroness, Super Hit and Yokkell — all profile as closers, yet the field contains far more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically settle at the rear; Beach Point, Skibo, Barry's Boy, Thankyou Baroness, Super Hit and Yokkell are redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the true back of the field will be thinned and several nominally hold-up types will end up closer than ideal. This shape — a lone leader controlling pace with a compacted midfield group tracking — favours horses that can travel prominently or in midfield without cover and then sustain their effort through the Epsom straight, rather than those who need a true end-to-end gallop to deliver a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bobacious Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable pace and the soft ground blunts the closers' late kicks.
scenarios.body: Bobacious dictates on his own terms, ensuring the pace is never genuinely testing enough to exhaust him, and the compacted hold-up field fails to generate sufficient momentum through the straight to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed horses settles close enough to the pace in midfield and picks off a tiring Bobacious inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The moderate tempo means a horse travelling in the first half of the field can conserve energy and produce a decisive run down the Epsom camber; Carnival Day and Patrol have soft-ground form and position themselves to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious sets a genuinely strong tempo from the front — perhaps rattled by pressure from riders pushing forward — and the soft ground brings true stayers into play.
scenarios.body: A draining pace off soft ground turns this into an endurance test, with horses like Moonrunner and Patrol — who have placed on soft — grinding past the field late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Free-for-All
scenarios.trigger: If Bobacious overcooks the early fractions or fails to stride out freely, collapsing before the straight and reducing the race to a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With no controlling influence, the race becomes chaotic and a fresh-legged horse hitting the line hard from behind — such as Super Hit or Yokkell, with recent winning form — could benefit from the scramble.

watchPoints.text: Bobacious — watch whether Liam Wright (3lb claimer) settles him into a controlled lead or allows him to bowl along too freely; if the pace is misjudged either way, the entire race shape collapses.

Beach Point, Skibo, Barry's Boy, Thankyou Baroness, Super Hit and Yokkell — all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map; watch in the early stages whether any of them are unable to get cover and end up racing wide or exposed, which would significantly reduce their winning prospects.

Carnival Day and Patrol — both have viable soft-ground form and will be travelling in the midfield group; if either gets a clean passage down the Epsom straight, they are the most naturally positioned to challenge Bobacious from off the pace.
Thankyou Baroness — 195 days off the track is a substantial absence; watch her in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of ring-rustiness or greenness before committing to her as a factor.

Super Hit — headgear and Cieren Fallon booking are positive pointers, but watch the going-report confirmation; the declared going of good-to-soft rather than soft may sharpen the pace enough to favour this horse if the ground rides quicker than expected.

races.name: Quickslide Quick Ride Apprentices' Derby Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Charmaine
runners_data.note: Won at 1m (Goodwood) on good and has strong place form at 12f, making this 1m4f trip a slight stretch, but James Fanshawe's yard is in decent form (4/20 over 14 days) and Arron D'Arcy's 7lb claim is a significant aid at the weights; prominent style suits this pace shape ideally.
runners_data.comment: Charmaine won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, making her conditions look well suited, and while 39 days between runs is a minor query, she arrives in decent heart and rates a confident pick at 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Gordon Grey
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, set to get a completely uncontested lead with no obvious challenger; recent soft-ground form is moderate (6th and 13th in two soft-ground starts) and the headgear (tongue-tie and pads) suggests he needs to be on-song, but dictating from the front is a genuine advantage here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our rating, Gordon Grey has run over today's trip and going and returns in good order just 10 days since his last start, but a winless recent run of form — including a sixth last time out — means he must prove he can translate promise into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Galaxy Star
runners_data.note: Won over 11f on standard going and Alan King's yard is firing (1/12 in 14 days with a winner); Harry Vigors claims 3lb and Galaxy Star's prominent style makes it well-suited to track Gordon Grey and strike in the straight, though the soft ground at Epsom represents a slight unknown on current form.
runners_data.comment: Galaxy Star won one in her last four starts and has run over today's trip, returning after 29 days carrying 136 lb — a lively each-way threat, though her two most recent efforts have been disappointing and she must bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: Has soft-ground experience and headgear (tongue-tie), but ran in only 0W/0P in similar conditions in recent history; races from hold-up, which is a structural disadvantage in a slow-run seven-runner field, and needs something to go wrong ahead of it to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Epictetus won three starts back and was third four starts back, showing he knows how to compete at this level, and carrying 135 lb off a sharp ten-day turnaround is the key question after two below-par efforts since.

runners_data.name: Naval Command
runners_data.note: Last ran 56 days ago for Ralph Beckett, whose yard has been very busy (9/48 in 14 days), and the tongue-tie is fitted; a hold-up runner with no wins or places from similar going in recent outings, and the long gap since its last start adds uncertainty about current condition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Naval Command faces a stiff task here; a return of three fifths, a ninth and a second five starts back makes for uninspiring recent form, though he has run over today's trip and going and experience at the weights may count for something.

runners_data.name: Duc De Kent
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old is a true hold-up horse whose position on the pace map has been redistributed to midfield — it is unlikely to secure that slot naturally and will probably race from the rear as usual; form figures of 590/60 show limited recent impact, and the style-fit discount is warranted given this race shape suits prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Duc De Kent has run over today's trip and comes here 29 days on from his last start, but winless in his last five outings and with the trainer striking at just 4% recently, he faces an uphill task despite a speed rating of 80 suggesting some ability.

runners_data.name: Crooked Path
runners_data.note: Recent form shows back-to-back wins (1/12f soft and 1/12f standard) and this 4-year-old with a hood fitted is arguably the most in-form runner in the field; Mason Paetel rides and the prominent style meshes well with this race shape — the step back to 1m4f from 1m6f/2m trips in its wins is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Crooked Path makes it hard to build a case, with two unplaced efforts in his last five starts before a revival two runs back; second last time out at least suggests freshness suits, and he has run over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Gordon Grey is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only seven runners on soft ground over 1m4f at Epsom, he is likely to set a measured, uncontested tempo from the front — no horse in this field has the profile or the mandate to challenge him for the lead early. Charmaine and Galaxy Star will press forward to prominent positions just behind, creating a small lead group that dictates the shape of the race, while Crooked Path may also try to race prominently given its headgear and recent front-running form. The soft going will suppress fractions and reward horses who can travel economically close to the pace rather than those who need a strong gallop to set up a late charge — Epictetus, Naval Command, and the redistributed Duc De Kent will need either the tempo to lift dramatically or rivals to crack early if they are to get into it from the rear. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel fluidly just off Gordon Grey's shoulder and pick him off in the straight, with pure hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage on a track where soft ground typically compresses the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Gordon Grey sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race is decided by who travels best close to the front.
scenarios.body: Gordon Grey leads at a soft-ground-compressed tempo, with Charmaine and Galaxy Star ideally placed to pounce turning into the straight, and Crooked Path also in contention from a prominent position; the slow-to-steady pace never generates the searching gallop that hold-up horses need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Out
scenarios.trigger: If Gordon Grey is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the pace is slow enough that he never gets headed.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to press him, Gordon Grey dictates every yard and the soft ground paradoxically suits his relaxed front-running style; a slow-run race into a long straight can catch chasers flat-footed if they leave the challenge too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is stronger than expected and the prominent horses overcook it entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Epictetus or Naval Command, racing with cover from midfield, could find the others weakening in the soft ground and pick them off late; this scenario requires the pace to be genuinely testing, which is not the likeliest read of a seven-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep Wins
scenarios.trigger: If a contentious pace breaks out between the front three and they collectively burn each other off.
scenarios.body: Duc De Kent, despite being mapped out of its natural position and carrying a style-fit discount, could theoretically benefit if chaos unfolds in front; this is the least likely shape given there is only one true front-runner and the redistribution tag confirms this scenario depends on horses racing well out of role.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Crooked Path's hood and recent double winning form means it presses Gordon Grey for the lead rather than settling in behind — if it does, it changes the race shape from uncontested to contested and could compromise Gordon Grey significantly.

Duc De Kent's style-fit discount is real — if it somehow does get a midfield position rather than its natural hold-up spot, watch whether it benefits unexpectedly, but do not overrate the chance given the redistribution tag.
Naval Command returns after 56 days off; watch the market and paddock for signs of wellbeing, as a first run back for a hold-up horse in soft ground over 1m4f is a demanding ask on fitness.

Galaxy Star's Alan King yard is in strong form (1 winner from 12 in 14 days) and Harry Vigors' 3lb claim reduces the weight meaningfully — watch for strong market support given the prominent style and course trip combination.

The going report confirms Good To Soft rather than Soft for the 3:42 race specifically, which slightly reduces the stamina premium and may allow a front-runner such as Gordon Grey to last longer than expected — watch for whether the track announcement shifts before race time.

races.name: Under Starters Orders For Fit Show 2027 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Virtue Diligence
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up filly from Amanda Perrett's yard who has placed at this trip on soft and artificial surfaces (headgear: hood), but her 0-from-6 record and lack of any win suggests she needs a very specific pace collapse to feature, and at OR 65 the rating is fair rather than lenient.

runners_data.name: Sullom Voe
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 3yo has a worrying pattern of fading in the finish (flagged), finishing no better than sixth in recent outings, and although the step up in trip via hold-up tactics gives a logical angle, that finishing weakness on a straight, soft-ground Epsom straight is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Sullom Voe has managed no better than sixth in her last four starts and arrives winless in that stretch, while her trainer has drawn a blank in 23 attempts over the past fortnight — though 31 days between runs suggests she returns fresh, and a weight of 135 lb is her burden to carry.

runners_data.name: Flag Of Eva
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's filly has shown some placed form over 10-11f on good ground but has a 54-day break to shake off, and a hold-up style on a track that can punish late runners means she needs a strong pace to maximise her run.
runners_data.comment: Flag Of Eva has been winless in his last four starts, with only a third two runs back to offer amid a pair of sixths, and a 54-day absence plus a rating that ranks him 12th of 15 make him very difficult to recommend here.

runners_data.name: Shirakawa
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's front-runner is the key pace figure in the race — two wins from the front over 10f on good ground and a trainer strike-rate of 3/36 over 14 days is modest, but the lack of any rival willing to press means she dictates; the slight concern is the step up from 1m2f to 1m4f on ground softer than her winning form.
runners_data.comment: Shirakawa arrives here on the back of back-to-back wins in her recent starts and followed that sequence with a runner-up finish, showing she has maintained her form well; the main risk is that a fourth last time out hints her peak may have passed.

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Tom Queally partners this D Donovan-trained hold-up filly who has placed on soft going over 9f previously (2/15 in similar going) but whose OR=64 form has trended downward, and the jump to 1m4f at Epsom for the first time is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Daretobedifferent catches the eye as the top-rated runner in this field, and her going experience is a clear asset; a winner in recent starts, she returns after 30 days off carrying 134 lb, with a fifth last time out the main reservation.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Interesting hold-up stayer from David Flood's yard who won at 1m4f on good ground and placed twice at 1m2f on good — the step back to this trip suits, and Kaiya Fraser retains the ride, though her 0-from-6 record on similar going and need for a proper pace-collapse tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Won two of her last six starts with a second one start back, but that fourth last time out tempers expectations slightly; has run over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh enough to go close again.

runners_data.name: Tenison
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's colt won at 1m2f on soft and has a legitimate claim on going and trip — naturally a hold-up horse whose instinct would place him further back than the midfield slot the crowded field forces upon him, which paradoxically could be helpful at Epsom where he needs to be in range at Tattenham Corner.
runners_data.comment: Tenison won on her second-most-recent start and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 77 marking her out as a serious threat in this field; the concern is that seventh last time out leaves her current form open to question.

runners_data.name: Blue Hill
runners_data.note: Ismail Mohammed & Jose Santos's lightly-raced 3yo has form only over shorter trips on standard and good going, making the jump to 1m4f on good-to-soft a step into the unknown; prominent style is a positional asset with Shirakawa, and Benoit de la Sayette is a sharp jockey around Epsom.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked 13 of 15 on our figures, Blue Hill faces a stiff task here; she has been running into mid-division finishes, though 28 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Eze Sur Mer
runners_data.note: Richard Newland & Jamie Insole runner returning from 98 days off — that layoff is significant and he was finishing mid-pack on good and soft over 10-12f before the break; his natural closing instinct means he runs in a more forward cluster than he'd ideally want given how many hold-up types are crammed into this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 98 days off, Eze Sur Mer faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 72 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Caraway
runners_data.note: William Haggas's consistent 3yo has placed at 1m4f on soft (3rd at Chester) and twice placed at 1m2f on good, with Cieren Fallon a strong booking — the horse's genuine form in similar conditions and a trainer in flying form (13/52 over 14 days) make him one of the more credible threats, even if his true hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield role here.

runners_data.name: Time To Sparkle
runners_data.note: James Keane's filly has been consistently placed over 10f on good/standard but has one run on soft (1/11, unplaced) — the prominent style is a genuine positional asset in this shape, though Harry Vigors (5) on a light apprentice claim is a risk factor in a field of 17 on a technical track.
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out, she also showed consistency with a second three starts back, though a fifth five starts back hints at vulnerability; going experience helps, but 132 lb is a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Darkest Red
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's gelding has a solid record of placings on soft and good-to-soft at 12-13f (placed twice on soft over 12f) and Pat Cosgrave is an experienced rider around Epsom; his natural close-finishing instinct is compressed into midfield here, which at least puts him closer to the action than his preferred deep position.
runners_data.comment: Darkest Red has been a model of consistency, finishing second on three occasions in recent starts, and he brings solid distance experience to the table — though yet to win in his last six, converting that placed form into a breakthrough is the key question.

runners_data.name: Antiquarian
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's 3yo has been soundly beaten in recent outings (5th, 6th, 10th) with no wins, and while hold-up tactics on soft over this trip is theoretically fine, the form figures do not inspire confidence; his true rear-of-field instinct is shifted forward into midfield by weight of numbers.
runners_data.comment: Antiquarian has been winless in her last four starts, though a fifth and sixth suggest she has not been far off the frame; 31 days between runs looks a fair enough freshener, but 130 lb is a stiff burden to carry back into form.

runners_data.name: Eshowe
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's filly has lost all three starts, finishing 10th-12th each time on standard turf, and carries a fading-in-finish flag — Georgia Dobie is a promising claimer but this profile offers very little encouragement for a first run on good-to-soft; she would naturally race furthest back but the field size forces her into a midfield position she is unlikely to exploit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 14 of 15 on our figures, Eshowe makes for a difficult proposition, though he has run over today's trip before and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Dijon Gone
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's gelding ran second on soft over 12f recently (2/12f/SOF) and this is his most recent piece of positive form — only 12 days since last run suggests freshness, and headgear (blinkers/hood noted) may help; naturally a hold-up type crammed into midfield, but the soft-ground placed form is a genuine angle worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Dijon Gone at least showed some spark with a runner-up finish last time out twelve days ago, and she has run over today's trip before; carrying 121 lb against a field of fifteen, her rating of 66 suggests more ability than her recent record implies, though consistency remains the question.

runners_data.name: Fletcher
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's 3yo won over 12f on good and placed twice at 12f on good or soft — there is a trip and form basis here, and the yard has a minor 14-day presence (1/14); his deeply held-up instinct is repositioned into midfield by the volume of closers in the field, and Jack Dace (5) claiming 5lb is a notable booking consideration in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Fletcher has winning form in his recent starts but has finished seventh twice and sixth once in that same spell, making consistency the issue; he has run over today's trip and going, and 44 days off keeps him fairly fresh, but ranked eleventh of fifteen on our figures he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's third runner in the race, a prominent-placed gelding (headgear: hood/visor) who placed at 12f on standard going and has shown consistency at similar trips — Tyler Heard takes the ride and the prominent style is a structural positive in this shape, though an OR of only 45 means he is significantly outrated.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Cormorant Rock is winless in his last six starts, with a latest third the sole crumb of comfort; he has run over today's trip before, but at a mark of 45 and carrying 116 lb, he faces a stiff task here.

races.paceDynamic: Shirakawa is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pressure for the lead — with Epsom's 1m4f trip beginning on the back straight before the famous descent into Tattenham Corner, a lone pace-setter who controls fractions on good-to-soft ground can dictate an honest but not brutal tempo. Blue Hill, Time To Sparkle and Cormorant Rock are the only other prominent-placed horses, meaning Shirakawa should settle comfortably in front and set a measured, sustainable gallop that does not invite a cavalry charge. The soft-ish ground will stretch the field out naturally on the climb and punish horses who burn energy fighting for position early, making it very difficult for the overcrowded hold-up brigade to find clear daylight in time. This race shape firmly favours the small cluster of prominent racers who can travel close to the pace without having to sprint from deep, as the likely single file through the turn will leave genuine closers with too much ground to make up. Several runners — Tenison, Eze Sur Mer, Caraway, Darkest Red, Antiquarian, Eshowe, Dijon Gone and Fletcher — are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for the field to accommodate naturally; of those, Caraway (Haggas, consistent form) and Tenison (Chapple-Hyam) are best placed to actually secure a workable midfield pitch rather than being trapped at the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shirakawa Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Shirakawa is allowed to bowl along in front at a controlled tempo with no rival willing or able to press from the outset.
scenarios.body: Shirakawa dictates every fraction through the back straight and down the hill, arriving at the home straight with an unspent engine and enough reserve to repel challengers on ground that suits a front-runner who has already shown a win at this trip on good; the prominent horses tucked in behind — Blue Hill, Time To Sparkle — are the primary beneficiaries of the slipstream, avoiding the energy cost paid by those forced wide or late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Shirakawa sets a pace that is slightly too strong and briefly leaves a gap for one of the prominent horses to swoop at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Caraway or Darkast Red, travelling closer to the pace than their natural style demands, find themselves in a sweet spot as Shirakawa's gallop catches up with it on the soft ground up the Epsom straight; a horse that has been held up marginally but within striking distance of the principals can produce a sustained late run without needing to find a seam through traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is fractionally too strong and the soft ground creates enough attrition to bring genuine hold-up horses into play inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Horses like A Daughters Love, who has course-relevant staying form at 12f on good, and Dijon Gone, who placed on soft at 12f recently, could theoretically finish powerfully if the field strings out and creates gaps down the rail; however, most true hold-up types here are operating in a compressed, crowded section of the field and face real traffic risks, limiting the probability of this shape fully delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If a slow or uneven early pace causes the large field to bunch through Tattenham Corner, creating a chaotic final two furlongs where position is luck.
scenarios.body: A muddling pace would ordinarily favour hold-up horses, but with so many of them clustered together and riding a course that naturally strings out the field, the traffic problem is severe; the horse most likely to profit from chaos is one with a wide, clean draw and a jockey (Cieren Fallon on Caraway, Benoit de la Sayette on Blue Hill) experienced enough to find the gaps quickly.

watchPoints.text: Shirakawa holds the race in her hooves — if she is allowed to slide into a lone lead with no challenge through the back straight, the entire field will be chasing her shadow; watch whether any of Blue Hill or Cormorant Rock push forward to test her early, because if they do not, the race is run to her tempo exclusively.

Caraway (Cieren Fallon, Haggas yard in form) is the most dangerous horse operating out of his natural position — watch at the start whether Fallon peels out wider to avoid early traffic and gives himself room to travel in mid-division rather than being squeezed on the rail with the cluster of genuine closers.

With 17 runners on soft ground at Epsom's 1m4f start, the first two furlongs on the back straight are a flashpoint for bunching and scrimmaging — any horse drawn wide or slow away risks losing multiple lengths before the descent, and horses like Antiquarian and Eshowe with poor recent form could create interference.

A Daughters Love holds an unexposed staying profile and her trainer David Flood has saddled winners at this trip — Kaiya Fraser needs to position her much closer to the pace than a pure hold-up rider would instinctively ride, and whether she achieves that in a field of 17 will determine her chance of featuring.

races.name: Business Pilot Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Arbaawy
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed in four of his last six starts including twice on similar going, but Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) reduces the weight burden; racing in 4th or 5th quartile of this field on OR=75 and at 37 days since last run, he will likely find himself in mid-division hoping for a strong pace that this race may not generate.
runners_data.comment: Arbaawy has been a model of consistency, finishing third last time out and third on two further occasions in his last six starts, and he has experience of both today's trip and going conditions. Winless in recent starts, but rated 89 and the one to beat here from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Wild Dahlia
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter in this field; Cieren Fallon for Haggas (in-form at 13/52 over 14 days) can dictate uncontested from flag to finish, and the soft ground she handles adequately (2/6 similar going) should not stop her conserving energy across this flat 1m½f trip — the key risk is whether a prominent-style horse racing out of natural role on a longer, softer surface can sustain the lead home.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a runner-up three starts back show Wild Dahlia is capable of mixing it at this level, but a sixth last time out tempers enthusiasm; she has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall six is the weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Steps up from 10f to 12½f here and has placed on soft going (2/9f/GOO); Harry Vigors (5lb claim) for the in-form Ollie Sangster yard, but a hold-up style in a race where the pace may be too steady for genuine closers limits the scope — the extra distance could theoretically suit but there is no evidence of form at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Mayaada has run over today's distance and going before, and she arrives fresh on a 12-day turnaround after a promising second three starts back — our rating of 82 suggests she holds strong claims here. The risk is that she has been out of the frame in her last two starts.

runners_data.name: Eastern Veil
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 122 days off the track, but Balding (12/60 14-day) runs horses back to form well and she has a winning run over 8f on Standard as a strong stamina foundation; her Prominent style suits this controlled-pace scenario ideally and if the layoff has sharpened rather than dulled her she rates a serious threat to the favourite.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts back give Eastern Veil a solid recent foundation, but she was well beaten last time out and returns after a 122-day absence, which clouds her fitness; has run over today's trip and carries 134 lb from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Island Bear
runners_data.note: Carries a hood (blinkers), has been running over 7-10f and steps up in trip here which may unlock stamina reserves; Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride and the horse has consistent placing form in the 4-7 bracket on similar going — a handy position off Wild Dahlia's pace is its most likely tactical slot and the trip extension could prove beneficial.
runners_data.comment: Island Bear arrives here just 15 days fresh, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 84 puts him second among the ten runners — a strong case that he is knocking on the door; the concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over 8f on Good going and freshly raced at 19 days; Hector Crouch keeps the ride for Michael Bell (2/21 14-day) and the horse's recent upward trajectory gives it credibility as an improver — a natural hold-up type that will need a proper pace to get competitive, which this shape may not supply.
runners_data.comment: Royal Bodyguard won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, which counts in his favour, but his speed rating of 69 trails several rivals and inconsistency — a sixth and an eighth in recent starts — is a concern at 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Likeness
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up racer placed on the map in midfield purely because the field contains too many true rear-runners; George Bass for Jack Channon (2/21 14-day) and the horse has a fine placed record (three seconds in recent five) but operates best from off a strong pace — the controlled tempo this race shape produces means conditions may not play to its strengths.
runners_data.comment: Likeness has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second three times in her last five outings, including second last time out just 20 days ago, and has run over today's trip; the main risk is she remains yet to win despite those bold displays.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with notable winning form at 8f (two wins in five) that has been shifted forward on the map rather than sitting at true rear; Rhys Clutterbuck for Gary & Moore (2/26 14-day) at 18 days since last run is workmanlike, and the horse's best form on Good going slightly concerns on today's softer surface — placed third on soft previously but yet to win on it.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, My Old Mate faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals, and his speed rating of 66 gives little encouragement; however, he does arrive in decent nick — second last time out — and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sail On Sailor
runners_data.note: Won twice over 8-10f on Good and Standard earlier this season but the last two runs have returned a fifth and sixth, and the 10-day turnaround is notably tight; a natural hold-up horse displaced forward on the map, Harry Davies takes the ride for Simon Dow, and the declining recent form string (311156) warrants caution even if the trip could theoretically suit.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and with a speed rating of 58 that makes him hard to fancy, Sail On Sailor does arrive on the back of three consecutive wins before his recent sixth and fifth, and he has experience over today's trip and going from stall two carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Fizzy Bear
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR=58 and form reads 50504 — no evidence of competitive threat at this level; Jack Dace (5lb claim) for George Baker and 31 days since last run, a genuine hold-up type repositioned forward on the map, but without the form or rating to suggest this represents anything other than a straightforward each-way outsider needing everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Fizzy Bear is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a reasonable 31-day break carrying 118 lb from stall 8.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Dahlia is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap over 1m½f on Good to Soft Epsom, and with no genuine rival to press her she is poised to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Cieren Fallon will be able to dictate terms and manage fractions, which on this relatively flat trip over soft ground typically sets up a steadily-run contest rather than a searching end-to-end test. The critical shape factor is that Eastern Bear and Island Bear will seek prominent berths to chase Wild Dahlia, but the field is loaded with horses whose natural mode is hold-up — Likeness, My Old Mate, Sail On Sailor and Fizzy Bear are all genuine hold-up types that have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they simply cannot all settle at the rear in a 10-runner field; of these, Sail On Sailor and My Old Mate have the form and fitness to press furthest forward from their natural positions. With a lone, uncontested pace-setter operating at a measured tempo on softening ground, this race shape strongly favours horses sitting just off the pace in prominent or close-midfield positions — those able to track Wild Dahlia without using excessive energy — rather than deep closers, who will need a strong tempo to get into the race that this shape is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Dahlia dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the winner tracks her in second or third without burning reserves.
scenarios.body: Wild Dahlia sets a sustainable fractions-controlled gallop and the closest pursuers — Eastern Veil and Island Bear — get the cleanest possible run through the early part of the race; on Good to Soft the premium is on those who travel well in the first half and sustain into the final two furlongs rather than those needing a fast early pace to get competitive. Horses sitting handy without fighting for position are perfectly positioned to pounce when Fallon kicks, and Eastern Veil's stamina profile at this longer trip gives her a strong theoretical claim.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Capitalises Fully
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Dahlia's uncontested lead and Fallon's ability to conserve energy throughout sees her simply outrun the field in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: A lone pacer who has controlled every yard and met no early pressure can be dangerously fresh entering the final two furlongs, particularly on a softer surface that rewards economical use of energy; Wild Dahlia won over 8f on Standard and placed twice on similar ground, and Haggas's strong 13/52 two-week strike rate supports an in-form yard delivering on the day. The redistribution of so many hold-up horses means no one will be coming from far back with a meaningful late surge, leaving the leader with clear air and no closing wave to fear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Dahlia sets a stronger tempo than expected and the race develops into a true test of stamina, opening the door for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Only under a genuinely searching gallop do horses that need to come from off the pace get the momentum they require over this trip; Royal Bodyguard is the most interesting of the hold-up brigade given recent winning form (1/8f/GOO) and a clean fitness profile at 19 days since last run, and Arbaawy has placed consistently in similar company. However, this scenario is deliberately discounted because the horses most likely to win it — Likeness, My Old Mate, Sail On Sailor — are all redistributed from their natural rearward positions, meaning they are unlikely to be ideally placed to deliver a genuine late burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Dahlia is challenged or stumbles early, breaking up the expected race shape and producing a muddled, erratic gallop.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine pace controller, the race could become falsely run in small groups with no horse travelling smoothly throughout; this is the least likely outcome given Wild Dahlia's confirmed front-running profile and the absence of any horse likely to seriously push her in the early stages. In this outlier scenario, a horse with tactical versatility like Eastern Veil — who has raced prominently and holds up with equal facility — would cope best with a disrupted rhythm.

watchPoints.text: Wild Dahlia sets uncontested pace — if Cieren Fallon is able to control fractions throughout and soft ground fails to blunt her stamina, she may be considerably more difficult to peg back than her OR=75 and recent form suggest.

Eastern Veil returns from 122 days off — monitor closely in the paddock and early in the race; a smooth traveller resuming for a powerful yard (Balding, 12/60) off a clean break can be deceptively well-handicapped, and any sign of freshness and fluency will make her extremely dangerous from her prominent position.

The cluster of hold-up horses redistributed to midfield — Likeness, My Old Mate, Sail On Sailor — creates a congestion risk in the early-to-middle stages; if any of these attempt to reclaim natural rear ground it could cause traffic issues for Royal Bodyguard and Arbaawy trying to find clear runs from behind.

Royal Bodyguard is the form horse on recent evidence (last-time-out winner, progressive profile) but watch whether Hector Crouch elects to push forward from a hold-up style rather than waiting for a pace that may not materialise — an aggressive tactical ride could transform its prospects in this shape.

Island Bear carries headgear (blinkers) for the first time or as a consistent headgear user — monitor its early behaviour and whether the blinkers sharpen its prominent style or cause it to overcook the early part of the race chasing Wild Dahlia's controlled gallop.

races.name: Feeling Flush With Emplas Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with soft-ground form (placed twice in similar conditions), trained by Gary & Josh Moore with Toby Moore claiming 7lb; needs a genuinely searching gallop to close from the rear and the uncontested pace of Tronido makes that harder to find; tongue-tie fitted.
runners_data.comment: Oj Lifestyle has been knocking on the door in his last two starts, finishing third on each occasion, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating putting him narrowly top of this field. The main concern is that he failed to convert that recent consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Mr Ubiquitous
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up markedly in trip from his last five runs which were all at 7f-8f; Harry Eustace's runner has one soft-ground placing from fifteen attempts in that ground but the extra distance here may unlock more stamina; drawn to track the pace from the off.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win from this kind of mark five starts back but has been held to fourth or worse in his last four, and at 135 lb from stall 1 he faces a stiff ask; he has run over today's distance and going, which at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: I Am Me
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-racing type whose last five runs were all on Standard (AW) surface and whose soft-ground experience is limited to three efforts at 8f on that ground; Cieren Fallon takes the ride and this is the first turf-soft test in this horse's recent sequence, which is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: I Am Me won three starts back and showed consistency with thirds in two of his last five starts, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset carrying 133 lb from stall 5; the risk is that back-to-back ninths since that victory raise a question over whether he can recapture that form.

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner, in good recent form (two wins in past 14 days for Simon Dow), with a strong record in soft going (3W3P from 4 starts); wears headgear (h) and returns quickly on 10 days rest; the uncontested lead on this trip and ground is his optimum scenario.
runners_data.comment: Tronido is in fine heart after winning last time out, and with experience over today's trip and going, conditions look right for her to go well again from stall two off 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Marsh Benham
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse who has placed once in soft-like conditions and whose last five runs on Good ground show consistency around the 8f mark; George Baker's runner steps up in trip from that recent form, and Jack Callan will be patient from the rear, needing a true pace to close.
runners_data.comment: Marsh Benham arrives here fresh enough on 18 days since his last outing, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour and a win three starts back giving his recent form a solid foundation; the risk is that his last two runs have yielded a sixth and a fourth, suggesting he needs to recapture that earlier spark under 132 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Post Rider
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing blinkers whose last five runs span soft, good and standard surfaces with a single placing in similar going; Mason Paetel claims 3lb and the horse's recent distance profile (up to 12f) suggests the 1m½f is within range, but closing from the rear against an uncontested leader is the challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Post Rider does at least bring distance experience and a return to form last time out with a third, though earlier finishes of sixth and eighth suggest inconsistency; 131 lb from stall three is her hand to play.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins in his recent form string (one on soft, one on good) and a lively trainer record (1W from 14 in the past 14 days for Jim Boyle); Donagh Murphy claims 5lb and with soft-ground placed form the step up to 1m½f on this ground looks broadly within his compass.
runners_data.comment: Play Me is ranked only seventh of nine on our figures, and his recent record — a ninth and a fourth sandwiched around a win two starts back — does little to inspire confidence; however, he returns on a quick turnaround just 10 days after that fourth and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Redredrobin
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine seasons with soft-ground know-how (5 starts, 2 places) but genuinely a hold-up horse by nature; the crowded rear of this field has pushed him into a midfield mapping that does not reflect how Malcolm Saunders' runner will actually race — Harry Vigors claims 5lb but getting a clear run from a compromised position is an extra hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a sixth last time out and little encouragement throughout recent outings, Redredrobin is hard to fancy despite carrying 119 lb from stall seven and having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's second string, another natural hold-up horse whose recent form runs of 6th and 3rd at 7f-8f on Standard suggest he wants a better surface than today's soft ground; Olivia Haines claims 7lb and, like Redredrobin, this horse's true racing position at the back of the field is busier than the map shows — the style compromise tempers his realistic chance significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Dandy Khan faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 13 days suggesting she is in decent order.

races.paceDynamic: Tronido is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, will stride into an uncontested position from the break and set a sustainable gallop over the 1m½f trip on Good to Soft ground at Epsom. Mr Ubiquitous, I Am Me, and Play Me will all press for prominent berths, creating some early positional friction behind Tronido but no serious threat to his lead, as none is likely to go past him into the front rank. The hold-up contingent — Oj Lifestyle, Marsh Benham, and Post Rider — will settle towards the rear on their own terms and depend on a strong enough pace to reel the leader in off the final bend. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race close to or on the pace, as Tronido's uncontested lead on soft ground is likely to see him control both tempo and margins, rewarding prominent runners who track him whilst leaving true closers with too much ground to make up. Redredrobin and Dandy Khan, genuine hold-up horses by style, have been mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; neither is likely to secure their natural position, and their chances are discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tronido Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tronido breaks cleanly and settles into a rhythm with no rivals pressuring him, setting a measured but sufficient gallop on the soft.
scenarios.body: Tronido dictates every yard from the front, controlling the pace to suit himself through the Epsom turns, and his soft-ground form (3W3P in similar conditions) gives him the profile to sustain it all the way to the line; horses who track him prominently will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Tronido's pace is sufficient to string the field out but one of the tracking prominent types picks him off in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mr Ubiquitous or Play Me, sitting a length or two off the leader through the home straight, benefits from the honest gallop without having had to lead, and the soft ground rewards their stamina over pure speed; both are versatile enough in style to make this transition.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to create a true test and one of the genuine closers finds clear running in the straight.
scenarios.body: Oj Lifestyle or Marsh Benham, settled quietly in the rear, would need the race to be run at a gallop that exhausts the front rank, but Epsom's track profile and Tronido's unchallenged lead make a true searching pace unlikely; this scenario is possible but structurally against the grain of this race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so conservative that the field concertinas entering the straight and the race becomes a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish would scramble the form book and hand an unexpected chance to a horse like Post Rider or Marsh Benham who possesses a sharp enough turn of foot for a short dash; however, this outcome is the least likely given Tronido's front-running profile and the soft ground conditions.

watchPoints.text: Tronido — watch the break; if Tyler Heard sends him straight to the front without being challenged, the race could be over as a contest by halfway given the soft ground and uncontested lead.
Mr Ubiquitous and Play Me — both want prominent ground, so watch for a positional duel in the first two furlongs that could see one or both use more energy than ideal before the turn.

Redredrobin and Dandy Khan — both are natural hold-up horses racing in a field where the rear is over-subscribed; watch whether either can find a clear passage in the straight or is forced to switch wide, costing ground on soft turf.

Post Rider — blinkers on a hold-up horse in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to bring him into it; if Tronido idles in front and the gallop drops, Mason Paetel may be forced to make an earlier move than suits this runner.

Oj Lifestyle — tongue-tie noted and returns on just 10 days rest; watch early behaviour and whether Toby Moore (7lb claim) can get the horse to settle cleanly before making the expected late run from the rear.
